Title: Baby boy found alive in US after believed buried for 24 hours, police say
Article:
SOUTH CAROLINA: An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South Carolina on Tuesday after he was believed to have been buried for about 24 hours, the Lexington County Sheriff's Department said.
The infant, Koah Sharpe, was found wrapped in a towel in a dog crate, shallowly buried in woods, according to the department.
"Certainly God is good. Just a few moments ago, we found little Koah, 11 months old, buried alive, clinging to life, crying — the most joyful sound you ever heard of a crying baby," Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said during a news conference.
Koon said the infant's father, Michael Comer, was arrested on Monday night on burglary and resisting arrest. The department is working with the solicitor's office to determine additional charges, he said.
Koah went missing on Monday after being left in his father's care at his mother's home while she ran an errand, Koon said. The boy was reported missing and authorities began a widespread search, according to the sheriff.
Koah was found after a search party discovered "freshly disturbed" dirt in the woods about 50 yards from Comer's father's house, Koon said.
The infant is currently at the hospital and will "hopefully" recover, the sheriff said.

Title: MetMalaysia issues strong winds, rough seas warning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected over several Malaysian waters, including those off the west and east coasts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, until 1pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
In a warning issued at 8.45am today, MetMalaysia said the affected waters include Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Perak and Selangor, eastern Johor, Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, as well as Sarawak and eastern Sabah, including Lahad Datu.
The conditions could bring winds of up to 50kmph and waves reaching 3.5m, posing a danger to small boats.
Meanwhile, MetMalaysia issued a third-category warning for northeasterly winds exceeding 60kmph and waves higher than 4.5m in Northeastern Condore and Northwestern Reef North until tomorrow.
A second-category warning was issued for Condore and parts of Reef North, while a first-category warning covers Palawan, Southeastern Reef North, Labuan, Layang-Layang, Samui and northern Tioman.
The department said rough sea conditions could endanger shipping and coastal activities, small craft and recreational sea activities, depending on the warning category.
A separate thunderstorm warning was also issued for several shipping areas, including the Straits of Melaka, Phuket, Samui, Tioman, Reef South, Condor, Bunguran, Sulu, Reef North, Palawan, Sulawesi, Layang-Layang and Labuan until 1pm today.

Title: Nine people seriously hurt in South Korea bus crash involving multiple vehicles
Article:
SEOUL: A bus crashed into multiple vehicles in the Bundang district of South Korea on Wednesday, leaving nine people seriously injured and 48 with minor injuries, according to the fire agency.
The bus struck the vehicles at around 7.34am (2234 GMT on Tuesday), including some waiting at a traffic light, before crashing into a median barrier, the National Fire Agency said, citing a witness.
The accident in Bundang, in Seongnam city south of Seoul, involved 32 vehicles, including four buses, a truck and 27 passenger cars, according to the agency.

Title: High inventories weigh on CPO, but 2027 outlook brightens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's record-high palm oil inventories could continue weighing on the commodity's near-term outlook, although analysts expect tightening supplies, weather-related production risks and stronger biodiesel demand to support crude palm oil (CPO) prices heading into 2027.
Palm oil inventories climbed for the seventh consecutive month to 3.62 million tonnes in October, up 3.2 per cent month-on-month, as higher opening stocks and increased production outweighed stronger exports.
Despite the inventory overhang, Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintained their "Overweight" calls on the plantation sector, citing expectations of tighter supply conditions and sustained CPO prices.
HLIB said elevated inventories were likely to persist in the near term as seasonally weaker exports could offset the anticipated slowdown in production from November.
"That said, a potential implementation of a palm oil export tax waiver could accelerate inventory drawdown more than currently anticipated," it said.
PublicInvest, however, expects inventories to begin easing from November as oil palm trees enter their seasonal low-production period.
Meanwhile, palm oil exports rebounded 55.7 per cent month-on-month to 1.71 million tonnes in October, marking their first monthly increase since July, supported by stronger shipments to Asia Oceania, the European Union and India.
However, export momentum weakened in early November, with Intertek Services reporting a 1.9 per cent month-on-month decline in shipments during the first 10 days.
On the supply side, Malaysian palm oil production rose 1.8 per cent month-on-month to 2.12 million tonnes in October, bringing output for the first 10 months of 2026 to 16.9 million tonnes, up 2.3 per cent year-on-year.
Looking ahead, both research firms expect seasonal production declines and the potential impact of El Nino to tighten palm oil supplies, while stronger biodiesel demand in Indonesia could further support prices.
"We maintain our 2026-2027 average CPO price assumptions of RM4,450 per tonne (2026) and RM4,500 per tonne (2027), supported by the anticipated tightening in the palm oil supply-demand balance as higher Indonesian biodiesel demand coincides with El Nino-related production losses."
PublicInvest noted that CPO prices had retreated almost 10 per cent this month following a correction in crude oil prices, which weakened the attractiveness of palm oil-based biodiesel.
Nevertheless, it believes the current weakness is unsustainable given tightening supplies in Indonesia and East Malaysia. It also highlighted the widening CPO-soybean oil price gap of US$325 per tonne, which could attract buying interest and help reduce Malaysian inventories.
For stock picks, HLIB favours Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd and IOI Corporation Bhd, with target prices of RM2.81 and RM5.16 respectively.
PublicInvest's top picks are Sarawak Plantation Bhd and Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, supported by dividend yields of 8.0 to 9.0 per cent and above-industry-average fresh fruit bunch production growth, with target prices of RM5.59 and RM8.55, respectively.
Both research firms expect tighter supply conditions and resilient demand to support the plantation sector's outlook into 2027 despite near-term inventory pressures.

Title: Loke makes final appearance with Transport Ministry staff
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former Transport Minister Anthony Loke attended the Transport Ministry's (MOT) monthly assembly for the last time today, following his resignation which took effect last night.
The Seremban MP's resignation took effect as soon as former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at his residence to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Loke also attended the Cahaya Madani event organised by the ministry in conjunction with Deepavali celebrations, marking one of his final appearances with MOT staff.
He was welcomed by Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and MOT secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.
His attendance at both events allowed ministry staff to gather and celebrate the festive occasion together.
Loke had earlier submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Sept 28 following the Pardons Board's decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

Title: Malaysia's industrial growth resilient despite AI headwinds: economists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's industrial growth will remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained global technology demand despite potential headwinds to the artificial intelligence (AI) investment cycle, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd.
Its economists Felicia Ling and Chong Lih Herng said the global technology upcycle would continue to anchor the country's industrial activity in the near term, while sustained strength in domestic demand would provide an additional buffer for the sector.
They said the latest industrial production data reflected improving momentum, with the industrial production index (IPI) expanding 6.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in September, up from five per cent in August.
The growth also exceeded the median consensus estimate of 5.6 per cent, driven by stronger manufacturing and electricity output, which more than offset a deeper contraction in mining production.
HLIB said the global manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) moderated slightly to 52.6 in October from 53 in September, while the output PMI eased to 53.1 from 53.8.
However, new orders, employment and new export orders remained close to recent peaks, while the inventory PMI pointed to rising stockbuilding activity.
"Despite emerging concerns over potential headwinds to the ongoing AI upcycle, we maintain our view that global tech demand will remain expansionary in the near term and continue to anchor Malaysia's industrial activity," the economists said in a note.
They added that strong growth momentum and inflationary risks heading into 2027 could also pave the way for monetary policy normalisation in the first half of next year, although the overnight policy rate (OPR) remained unchanged in 2026 as anticipated.
"While the OPR was left unchanged in 2026 as anticipated, strong growth momentum and inflationary risks heading into 2027 could pave the way for policy normalisation in the first half of 2027," they said.
On the September IPI performance, manufacturing output grew 9.4 per cent, accelerating from 7.4 per cent in August, while electricity production expanded 10.7 per cent against nine per cent previously.
In contrast, mining production contracted 9.4 per cent, compared with a 7.4 per cent decline in August, as lower natural gas and crude petroleum output weighed on the sector.
The manufacturing sector's stronger performance was broad-based, with export-orientated industries growing 10.6 per cent, compared with 9.9 per cent in August, while domestic-orientated manufacturing accelerated to seven per cent from 2.3 per cent.
Within the export-orientated segment, electrical and electronics (E&E) goods production expanded 17.3 per cent, slightly higher than the 16.9 per cent recorded previously.
This was consistent with the robust performance of E&E exports, which surged 69.2 per cent in September, compared with 66.5 per cent in August.
Other export-orientated industries also recorded stronger growth, including wood, furniture, paper products and printing, which expanded 6.1 per cent, while textiles, wearing apparel, leather products and footwear returned to growth at three per cent.
Meanwhile, petroleum, chemical, rubber and plastic products grew 2.7 per cent, against 2.6 per cent in August.
The domestic-orientated segment also recorded a marked improvement, supported by a turnaround in transport equipment and other manufacturing, which grew seven per cent after contracting 1.4 per cent previously.
Motor vehicle production rebounded 10.6 per cent following a 5.3 per cent decline in August, partly reflecting a low-base effect from maintenance shutdowns in September last year.
Food, beverages and tobacco production expanded 7.2 per cent, compared with 1.5 per cent previously, while non-metallic mineral, basic metal and fabricated metal products grew 6.8 per cent against 5.7 per cent.

Title: CoreWeave targets 2028 profitability as AI demand surges
Article:
NEW YORK: CoreWeave said on Tuesday it would become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028, as the AI cloud company sought to reassure investors that strong demand and customer commitments will support its debt-fuelled expansion.
Shares of the Nvidia-backed company were up 5.0 per cent in extended trading after it also said it does not see any material risks to its data-center buildout from a potential shift in regulatory landscape after the Democrats' sweeping win in the US midterms.
CoreWeave shares have crashed more than 40 per cent in the past month after the firm emerged as the focal point of growing AI bubble fears, with investors worried about heavy borrowing for setting up data centers against the backdrop of rising interest rates and the pace of returns on the massive investments.
The steep selloff also triggered a broader crisis of confidence in the AI trade. Earlier in the day, AI juggernaut Anthropic kicked off a roadshow for its share sale at a lower target valuation than earlier estimates.
Easing some jitters, Core Weave said it would not tap unsecured debt markets at current yields and that it had enough cash flow from existing customer commitments to repay current debt and any additional borrowing needed to fulfil those contracts.
CoreWeave had about US$46.9 billion in total debt as of the end of September. It expects to raise less than US$5 billion in additional capital through 2027.
CEO Mike Intrator said the company had US$9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits that will flow in over the next three months.
"Customer contracts come first, and investment follows. Because CoreWeave's investments are tied to committed demand, lenders have something concrete to lend against, and customers typically help fund the buildout," he said in a statement.
CoreWeave's revenue backlog stood at US$132.5 billion at September's end, rising from US$104 billion at the end of June. At the same time, its quarterly capital spending jumped to US$14.5 billion from US$9.4 billion in the prior quarter.
That spending is necessary to bring capacity online to meet the surging demand, Core Weave said it is largely sold out of capacity through the next year, with about ten times as much demand as available capacity.
NO IMPACT EXPECTED FROM CHANGES IN POLITICAL LANDSCAPE
Investors have been worried about tech companies' data centre expansion plans as they prepare for a tougher regulatory environment after the Democratic win in the midterm elections. Public backlash has already been growing in the US around data centres' impact on local resources, including water and power.
"There is going to be a lot more scrutiny on how you build, how you use resources... But I don't think it's going to require a material change in how we go about building our infrastructure. I don't think it's going to materially distort the costs of the buildout," Intrator told Reuters in an interview.
"I do think that there is going to be a pacing issue, as people need to be more transparent and work through the process with the communities and that's going to be prevalent across the industry. But that's how we've done it historically and it has been a hallmark of how we've built our data centres."
Intrator said that CoreWeave will not ramp up international expansion plans because of the election results.
"This is not a new strategy that you've got us building into as a reaction to the elections. This is something that we have been working at diligently for a year and a half already," he said.
CoreWeave now expects 2026 revenue to be between US$13.0 billion and US$13.3 billion, from US$12.4 billion to US$13.2 billion earlier.
It also lifted the lower end of its annual spending target by US$2 billion, now projecting spending of US$37 billion to US$39 billion.
CoreWeave's third-quarter revenue surged nearly 170 per cent to US$3.66 billion, beating estimates of US$3.55 billion, while a per-share loss of 95 cents came in smaller than estimates for a US$1.16 loss, according to data from LSEG.

Title: Malaysia must bolster cyber resilience as Europe supermarket attacks expose risks - Experts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to strengthen its operational cyber resilience, as recent attacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in Europe have exposed vulnerabilities in connected systems that could disrupt food supply chains, according to a cyber security expert.
Adjunct Professor of Cybersecurity Practice at the University Malaysia of Computer Science and Engineering (UNIMY), Murugason R. Thangaratnam, said attackers did not need advanced hacking skills, as everyday connected systems, such as refrigeration controllers, building management systems and monitoring platforms, were built for convenience and uninterrupted operation rather than security.
"So once they (appliances) are online, they become part of the attack surface. So this is one of the biggest gaps we seem to be having at the moment. It is how operational technology (OT) security is converging with information technology (IT) security.
"Refrigeration falls under OT technology, and I think this is something that the government and industry are trying to address because the OT side is still a big gap," he said when asked whether a similar cyberattack could happen in Malaysia during an interview on Bernama TV's Bernama World programme titled "Europe's Supermarket Cyber Threat", on Tuesday.
A series of cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration units across Europe has forced stores to dispose of spoiled food.
https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2026/11/1569396/fridge-cyberattack-hits-supermarkets-across-europe
According to reports, hundreds of supermarkets in France was hit by the attack in October after hackers gained control the software regulating the temperatures of refigeration units. This was followed by similar attacks on supermarkets in several European countries in early November.
Meanwhile, Murugason said the use of similar systems and remote monitoring platforms across retailers could expose multiple businesses to the same vulnerabilities, particularly when third-party vendors and service providers were involved.
"So that's the real concern. One weakness, repeated across many sites. The risk sits in the supply chain, and the fix has to include vendors and service providers, not just supermarkets," he said.
On how hackers could gain control of refrigeration systems, Murugason said weak default passwords and internet-exposed devices could allow attackers to access connected equipment by posing as authorised users, potentially enabling them to alter temperature settings or disable alarm systems.
"There does not have to be any sophisticated malware attack; it's as simple as that. Default passwords like 1234 are public knowledge, and even without that default password, publicly available search engines like Shodan can find exposed devices in minutes," he said.
He said that most Malaysian retailers and cold-chain operators used similar connected systems that were remotely managed by third parties, meaning they might not be immune to similar cyberattacks.
While acknowledging the efforts of the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and other agencies in developing the country's cyber security framework, he stressed that Malaysia needs to move beyond compliance towards strengthening operational resilience.
"In practice, we need to know what is connected and have visibility over what is connected, remove default passwords and public exposure, and have manual fallback plans. That means we need to go back to a pre-digital workflow. We must be ready for that, but it must be tested.
"Any fallback plan, if it's not tested, is not a plan, and we need to hold vendors accountable. Security has to be at every level along the chain, from the main contractor or the main buyer all the way down the supply chain. So we need to be prepared, not panic," he added.

Title: Microsoft presses Trump to scuttle ban on Chinese data centre tech
Article:
WASHINGTON: Microsoft and other companies and trade groups have pressed the Trump administration to halt plans to bar imports from China of a key component used in AI data centres, three people familiar with the situation said.
Reuters reported in August that the Trump administration wants to ban US imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fibre-optic cables at the speed of light within data centres. The concern is that they could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at US data centres.
Microsoft has 35 data centres under construction in the US and another 134 planned, according to Cleanview, a market intelligence company which tracks data centre development. It is one of a group of companies and trade groups making the case to the Trump administration that such a ban could irreparably damage the US edge over China in the AI race by further slowing the data centre rollout, the sources said.
The cloud and software company was one of a handful of firms that met with officials from the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council weeks after the Reuters report to flag the supply chain challenges that any such ban would present, two of the sources said.
"It really threatens to arguably grind (the data centre rollout) to a halt," said John Miller, Executive Vice President of Policy and General Counsel of the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI), a tech lobbying group, which has publicly urged the administration not to move forward with a ban.
He said many cloud companies have already purchased the AI chips needed for the buildout. "Those chips, without optical transceivers, literally could just sit there waiting around un-utilised until you actually have the transceivers to essentially connect them together," he added.
Some data centres need millions of optical transceivers to connect servers, routers and switches.
The Federal Communications Commission, which oversees the US ‌telecom industry, is working on the ban.
The efforts by Microsoft and other firms, which have not been previously reported, show how the agency's deliberations have set off alarms in an industry scrambling to meet surging demand for cloud and AI services despite a growing backlash by consumers over rising energy costs and water use.
Microsoft declined to comment. The White House and the FCC did not respond to requests for comment.
Beijing "firmly opposes the US overstretching the concept of national security and abusing state power to unjustifiably suppress Chinese companies," the Chinese embassy in Washington said in a statement. "China will continue to firmly safeguard the lawful rights and interests of Chinese companies."
U.S. COMPETITORS LACK SCALE
China boasts two-thirds of the global market for optical transceivers, according to Counterpoint Research. Chinese firms like Eoptolink and Zhongji Innolight, which was added to the Pentagon's list of Chinese military-backed companies, dominate global supply, counting top American hyperscalers among their customers.
US-based Coherent and Lumentum produce technology that competes with them but lacks the scale to replace Chinese vendors, according to a report by the Foundation for American Innovation.
"A Pentagon-listed Chinese military company, including Zhongji Innolight, should not be wiring America's data centres," the House Select Committee on China, led by Republican John Moolenaar, said in a social media post following the report. The FCC should "move forward and keep new (China)-linked optical transceivers out of our networks," the committee added.
Zhongji Innolight did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
ITI sent a letter to the FCC on Aug 13 calling on the telecoms watchdog to "refrain from adding optical transceivers" to a trade blacklist, emphasising the "potential effects that supply disruptions could have on data centre deployment and US AI leadership."
Morgan Stanley said in an October client note that the Trump administration was considering barring Chinese optical transceivers capable of handling 3.2 terabits of data per second, whose production is not expected to ramp up until 2028, with widespread installation expected in 2029.
Such a threshold could avoid antagonising US companies and Beijing while giving US optical companies time to expand production.
The FCC has not addressed the optical transceiver issue publicly, but two of the sources said the 3.2 terabit per second threshold is under consideration.
Lawmakers may not want to wait. In September, a bipartisan group of US lawmakers introduced legislation to bar the federal government from equipping sensitive government systems with Chinese-made optical transceivers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Article:

Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said firefighters were deployed to the scene following a distress call at 12.40am.

Title: Australia home loans plunge 15.5pct in September quarter amid investor exodus
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia recorded a record drop in new home loans in the September quarter as higher borrowing costs and proposed changes to taxes on investment cut demand, another sign interest rate hikes were working to slow the economy.
Wednesday's data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed total new home loans fell 15.5 per cent by value in the September quarter to A$81.16 billion (US$55.6 billion), for a third straight quarter of declines.
The number of loans dropped 15 per cent in the quarter.
Loans for owner occupiers fell 5.3 per cent by value, while those for investment properties dropped a steep 32.3 per cent.
The ABS said the headline drop of 15.5 per cent was the largest quarterly fall since data began in late 2002, driven by investors.

Title: Nvidia faces deepening scrutiny over China chip ties, CEO affair
Article:
NEW YORK: Nvidia shed about US$430 billion in market value over two sessions as new reports deepened questions about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
The controversy escalated on several fronts on Tuesday as allegations emerged that Huang's relationship with Alice Huang aided at least US$7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China and that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had previously briefed President Donald Trump on the affair.
Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer demanded answers from the administration and tighter curbs on chip exports to China, while the company's independent directors hired outside counsel to investigate.
The allegations have turned Huang's personal conduct into a broader risk for Nvidia, raising questions about the company's governance and its dependence on the chief executive officer (CEO) who has led it for more than three decades and built it into the dominant supplier of AI chips. He owns about 3.6 per cent of the company — but does not have majority voting control — and runs an unusually flat organisation in which dozens of executives report directly to him.
The FBI is separately examining whether 63-year-old Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife but provided no details about the relationship. China's foreign ministry has said the spy accusations are "groundless".
Huang apologised to top executives at a closed-door meeting on Monday before pivoting to business and was back holding meetings at Nvidia's headquarters on Tuesday, CNBC reported.
Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe US national security or company secrets were compromised and that Huang has committed to cooperating with the internal review. The board has retained Joon Kim, a Wachtell Lipton partner and former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York, whose practice includes internal investigations and white-collar defence, to lead the probe.
Nvidia's stock, which had been nearly flat this year before news of the affair broke, has fallen 9.5 per cent since then. The shares have lagged the broader market on investor unease over whether massive spending on AI will deliver adequate returns.
WHEN DID TRUMP KNOW?
The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Rubio had briefed Trump aboard Air Force One en route to China in May about US intelligence indicating Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
Trump said on Monday he had spoken with Huang and asked whether he knew the woman was a spy. Trump said Huang told him he had "absolutely no idea" and that he believed the Nvidia CEO.
Trump also said he had not known about the alleged ties when Huang accompanied him to China in May.
A White House official disputed the report and referred Reuters to Trump's comments on Monday.
Schumer said on Tuesday that Congress must have a full accounting of Trump's defence of Huang and called on lawmakers to quickly approve new restrictions on US chip exports to China.
"He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends," Schumer said, accusing Trump of failing to address foreign espionage in the American technology industry.
US news publication Axios, citing sources, reported on Tuesday that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was sent a highly classified memo warning about the Nvidia CEO's relationship with Alice Huang.
Reuters could not immediately verify that report. The Commerce Department and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours.
WHO IS ALICE HUANG?
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information reported.
When orders for Nvidia chips subject to US export restrictions stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report. Some of the chips ultimately served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs.
Reuters could not determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.
She held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, which was linked to Century Litong, a China-based company that secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia in 2023, giving it priority access to the company's chips.
Separately, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday that several US government agencies pushed for Megaspeed to be included on the entity list, a trade blacklist of groups connected to China that US officials say pose national security risks, but the US Commerce Department was delaying efforts to blacklist the company.
The Commerce Department had sought more information about some companies under consideration, the FT reported. It was unclear whether Megaspeed was among those companies, but the delay has left it off the list, according to the report.
The US Department of Commerce and Nvidia did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed and Century Litong were not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kennedy family tries to stop Trump's Washington arch
Article:
Several members of the Kennedy family, one of America's most famous political dynasties, filed on Tuesday to join a court case aimed at stopping President Donald Trump from building a proposed triumphal arch in Washington, saying it would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' grave sites.
The 250-foot (76-metre) arch, shown in a rendering to include a flame held by a 60-foot gold winged female figure and flanked by gold flying eagles, would be situated across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial on a highway roundabout near the entrance to the Arlington National Cemetery.
A judge has already issued a temporary order blocking construction through Nov 19 as she considers whether to issue a preliminary injunction.
The arch "will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sight lines to the existing grave sites and memorials established in the Kennedy family's honour at Arlington National Cemetery, as well as to the memorials of hundreds of thousands of fallen American heroes," the filing said.
The Kennedy family is one of the most prolific political dynasties in US history, notably including former President John F. Kennedy. Trump's health secretary is Robert F. Kennedy Jr., nephew to the assassinated former president.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
The Trump administration contends Congress approved the arch more than 100 years ago when it also authorised construction of a bridge across the Potomac River. It has said that the arch would honour veterans.
Numerous Democrats in Congress have vowed to block construction once they take control in January, after winning November's midterm elections.

Title: Kelantan fire dept mulls 48-hour shifts for major flood operations
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department is considering extending the duty shifts of its personnel to up to 48 hours in the event of major flooding during the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), to strengthen its rescue operation capabilities.
Its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan, said the measure could involve adjustments to the current shift system, from 12-hour rotations to 24- or 48-hour shifts, depending on operational requirements and the situation on the ground during a disaster.
He said personnel currently work in three teams on a 12-hour shift system to ensure fire station operations continue around the clock.
"To increase the number of personnel available during major floods, we will manage leave and switch from 12-hour to 24-hour shifts, thereby increasing the number of personnel on duty," he told Bernama recently.
He said a freeze on leave could also be imposed, depending on the severity of the disaster, to ensure sufficient manpower, particularly when rescue operations require the deployment of more personnel.
However, the availability of assets, including boats, trucks and four-wheel-drive vehicles, was equally important to operational effectiveness, as increasing manpower alone would not be sufficient without the necessary equipment, he said.
In a related development, Kelantan fire department has identified vulnerable groups, including the elderly, persons with disabilities (PwDs) and bedridden patients living in flood-prone areas, to facilitate evacuation efforts in the event of flooding.
Farhan said the exercise was carried out in coordination with the State Disaster Management Committee, involving the Welfare Department and the Health Department.
He added that information on residents requiring special assistance during evacuation, including the number of elderly people and persons with disabilities in high-risk areas, had been compiled to support operational planning.
"We have identified the number of PwDs and elderly people in these areas who require attention, and the matter has been coordinated at the State Disaster Management Committee level," he said.
He said the actual evacuation process would depend on prevailing conditions when a disaster occurred, particularly during its initial stages, which were usually challenging for rescue agencies.
He added that training and inter-agency cooperation were also crucial to ensuring the safe and orderly evacuation of vulnerable groups.
On Sunday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a caution-level warning for continuous rain in several areas in Kelantan, Pahang and Sabah, as well as throughout Terengganu, effective until today.
MetMalaysia said the affected areas in Kelantan included Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Baru, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli.
Following the warning, the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage indicated that nine districts in Kelantan could potentially experience flooding during the same period.

Title: House Democrats to investigate Trump's handling of US spy agencies
Article:
WASHINGTON: Democrats in the US House of Representatives, who will control key committees next year, are preparing investigations into what they say was President Donald Trump's politicisation and gutting of US spy agencies, including whether analysts have censored themselves to avoid retaliation.
"There's absolutely evidence that analysts are hesitant to write on topics that they think might be controversial.
"There's absolutely evidence of a decline in morale in the analytic community because of the pressures that they are under," US Representative Jim Himes, a Connecticut Democrat who will become chairman of the House intelligence committee in January, told Reuters on Tuesday.
There has been little scrutiny of the state of the US intelligence community by the Republican-run Congress during the first two years of Trump's second term, during which the administration fired or forced out hundreds of officers and disrupted the production of analyses on key issues, including Iran.
Himes said that would change after he takes over the committee in January, when Democrats assume control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following their sweep of the November 3 midterm elections.
He did not disclose how the investigations would proceed, but said that one focus would be what he called retaliatory firings.
"We're going to tell the story of the patriots who were fired because they said something that was inconsistent with what the president wanted to be true," Himes said.
Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard last year cut her agency's staff by about 40%. CIA Director John Ratcliffe publicly pledged to reduce his workforce by more than 1,000 positions over several years.
Both offered deferred-resignation programmes that provided pay and benefits for employees who chose to leave.
The cuts included the firings of longtime intelligence analysts and officers from top posts, including at the National Intelligence Council, the analytical group overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.
At least two of those fired were analysts involved in an assessment that contradicted the White House's official policy on Venezuela.
The reductions have been viewed inside the intelligence agencies as a continuation of Trump's campaign against what he called the "deep state," a move critics say has drained the community of experience and expertise.
Reuters previously reported that some of Gabbard's projects affiliated with her Director's Initiative Group, a task force that revisited the 2020 election and the origins of Covid-19, created tensions inside the intelligence community.

Title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, flat against greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against major currencies but remained flat against the US dollar amid renewed expectations of a possible US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike following stronger-than-expected inflation data.
At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.0540/0590 against the greenback, unchanged from Tuesday's close of 4.0540/0580.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said US inflation data had heightened concerns over further monetary tightening, with the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 0.4 per cent month-on-month in October, above the consensus estimate of 0.3 per cent.
He said the prospect of higher interest rates also pushed yield on the two-year US Treasury note up by 18 basis points to 4.74 per cent, while the US Dollar Index strengthened 0.57 per cent to 102.233 points.
"Fed Governor Christopher Waller indicated that a 50 basis point hike could happen when the Federal Open Market Committee members reconvene on Dec 8 and 9, while Dallas Fed President Larrie Logan sees at least a two-quarter-point rate hike as necessary.
"As such, the ringgit could be experiencing downward pressure following the overnight trend in the US market. The US dollar-ringgit pair could trade within an RM4.06 to RM4.08 range today," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded firmer against a basket of major currencies.
It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5540/5573 from 2.5642/5669, appreciated vis-a-vis the euro to 4.5275/5331 from 4.5514/5559 and strengthened against the British pound to 5.4109/4175 from 5.4425/4479 at Tuesday's close.
The ringgit, however, traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It improved against the Singapore dollar to 3.1627/1669 from yesterday's close of 3.1726/1758 and climbed against the Thai baht to 12.0561/0800 from 12.1337/1497. It was almost flat vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah at 224.4/224.8 from 224.4/224.7 and was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.44/6.45.

Title: Social media age verification, travel restrictions among focus of today's Dewan Rakyat sitting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The enforcement status of social media age verification and restrictions on overseas travel were among the issues in focus at the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper published on the Parliament's official website, Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) will ask the communications minister about the enforcement status of social media age verification since June 1, as well as action against platforms that had yet to implement the verification process and the status of the six-month transition period, during the question-and-answer session.

Title: Tighter scrutiny expected on Malaysia as Nvidia scandal spills over
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia could face tighter scrutiny by the United States over advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chip shipments following allegations that Nvidia graphic processing units (GPUs) were diverted to China, although a blanket ban on supplies is unlikely for now.
Economists Business Times spoke to opine that the development could prompt Washington to strengthen export licensing requirements, end-user verification and shipment monitoring to prevent advanced semiconductor technology from reaching China through third countries.
"The bigger concern is whether Malaysia's reputation as a trusted semiconductor and technology hub could be affected, potentially making access to advanced AI chips more costly and time-consuming," BIMB Securities chief economist Imran Nurginias told Business Times.
Malaysia is embroiled in a controversy surrounding the relationship between Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy trying to get advanced AI technology from the US.
Alice was alleged to have founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, which had been investigated by authorities in the US and Singapore over suspected breaches of US export controls over advanced AI chips to China.
The issue has also drawn attention to Malaysia following reports linking Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, to the supply chain.
Julia Goh, senior economist at United Overseas Bank's Global Economics and Markets Research said this episode puts third-country data centres squarely back in Washington's spotlight.
But following the latest news, the US Congress is more likely to pass legislation aimed at tightening China's access to AI chips in light of the latest developments.
She added that the US would likely require businesses to track their chips to combat smuggling and push allies to restrict more chipmaking to China. Following the latest news, the US Congress is more likely to pass legislation aimed at tightening China's access to AI chips.
"We think the more likely outcome is not a hard cap on Malaysia's chip supply, but tighter conditions on how chips are used once they land: stronger end-user checks, and location tracking," said Goh.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd's economist Dr Afzanizam Abdul Rashid also expects the US Congress to push for legislation restricting China's access to advanced AI chips, with businesses potentially required to track shipments more closely to prevent smuggling.
He said a more hawkish stance towards China on technology and national security matters could emerge when the newly elected Congress takes office in January 2027.
"I would expect greater scrutiny from the US. The recent scandal with Nvidia is the direct link with China, as there is a security issue that may warrant further investigation," he said.
As it is, the investigation on Section 301 Trade Act 1974 on excess capacity in the semiconductor is still ongoing, added Afzanizam.
Despite the concern over tighter scrutiny by US authorities on companies operating in Malaysia, Goh said that Malaysia's enforcement track record is credible, having introduced permit requirements for US chip shipments and carried out customs seizures.
DATA CENTRE PIPELINE
On the implications for Malaysia's data centre industry, Imran of MBSB Research said he does not expect an immediate impact on the country's investment pipeline, particularly for projects with legitimate end-users and transparent procurement arrangements.
However, tighter export controls could increase procurement costs, delay the deployment of advanced GPUs and affect project timelines.
"More importantly, prolonged uncertainty could influence future investment decisions, particularly among global hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers," he said.
He added that Malaysian companies involved in the Nvidia supply chain were also likely to face closer scrutiny from US and local authorities.
Companies with strong governance and supply-chain controls should be better positioned to manage the risks, he said, adding that Malaysia's ambition to become a regional AI and data centre hub should not be compromised by weaknesses in export-control enforcement.
SNS ONLY SUPPLIES TO LOCAL DATA CENTRES
Meanwhile, SNS Network Technology Bhd, which is involved in Nvidia's GPU supply in Malaysia, stressed that all Nvidia GPU servers it procured are intended for Malaysian data centre projects, and not exported overseas.
Its group managing director Ko Yun Hung said that SNS conducts due diligence on customers, including checks on their backgrounds, ownerships, intended use, end-user and deployment locations.
"We take export-control compliance seriously and conduct due diligence on our customers, including their background, ownership, intended use, end-user and deployment location," he said.
Ko added that the company also assessed potential onward-transfer and diversion risks to ensure compliance with applicable regulations.
SNS is part of the Nvidia Partner Network (NPN) as a solution provider, supplying AI infrastructure and solutions to Malaysian businesses and organisations.
Its activities include supplying complete AI server solutions to data centres and enterprises, as well as operating its own AI infrastructure, the SNS AI Factory.
Launched in March 2025 in collaboration with Nvidia and Dell Technologies, the facility is located at Telekom Malaysia's Klang Valley Data Centre in Cyberjaya.
It is equipped with 64 Nvidia Hopper GPUs across eight Dell PowerEdge XE9680 servers.
Through the facility, SNS provides GPU-as-a-Service to enterprises, government agencies and research institutions, allowing customers to access high-performance computing resources locally.
Ko said the company's annual GPU procurement varied according to customer demand and project requirements, rather than a fixed import volume.
"Our GPU procurement varies from year to year, depending on customer demand, project requirements and the types of AI servers being deployed.
"We do not work towards a fixed annual import volume, as procurement is generally tied to confirmed orders and the specifications required for each project," he said.

Title: UK arrests US army member suspected of spying for Russia
Article:
LONDON: A member of the US military was arrested in Britain on Tuesday on suspicion of spying for Russia, London police said.
"The 41-year-old man was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday," London Metropolitan police said in a statement, adding that "The country to which the allegations relate is Russia."
The suspect was a member of the US Army and was being held at a London jail, police said, adding that they worked closely with US authorities on the case.
"This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities," Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing at the Met, was quoted as saying in the statement. "The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing."
"The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent," Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, said in the statement.

Title: Thomas Markle ordered back to jail after cutting off his ankle bracelet
Article:
LOS ANGELES: Thomas Markle, an accused child sexual predator and the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex Meghan Markle, was ordered back to jail on Tuesday after cutting of an electronic monitoring device he was supposed to wear as a condition of home confinement, federal prosecutors said.
US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Saxe Griffin ordered the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry returned to federal detention without bond at a hearing in Tampa, Florida, according to the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles, where the case against him is pending.
Thomas Markle was arrested and charged on Friday on a single federal count of possessing child sexual abuse material, including two explicit photographs of himself posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress.
According to an FBI affidavit filed in court as part of the criminal complaint lodged against Markle, federal agents seized the material in question, part of a cache of slides, film negatives and books, from storage units Markle had rented in Los Angeles since 2008.
Commenting on the case on Friday, FBI Director Kash Patel said Markle "targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."
Markle was most recently residing at an assisted living facility in Lakeland, Florida, near Tampa.
No plea was entered during Markle's initial court hearing last Friday, and the judge permitted him to be released from custody on condition that he submit to home detention and the wearing of a monitoring device.
But federal prosecutors on Monday asked the judge to revoke home-release and keep him detained in custody pending trial after he cut the ankle bracelet off overnight, and Griffin granted prosecutors' request.
Griffin on Friday also ordered Markle to undergo a psychiatric evaluation to determine whether he was mentally competent to face prosecution.
She cited her own reasonable cause to believe Markle was suffering from some mental deficiency, based in part on his advanced age and a "lack of recall" he demonstrated during his court appearance.

Title: US lawmakers urge new Epstein investigations in damning report
Article:
WASHINGTON: US lawmakers called for further criminal investigations into associates of notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, in a scathing report blaming prosecutors, financial institutions and powerful connections for allowing his abuse to continue for years.
The Epstein saga has dogged President Donald Trump, who was friends with the financier for years but has denied any knowledge of his crimes.
Accusations that Trump covered up much of the investigation triggered the first major rift with the president's support base after he returned to the White House.
The Republican-led House Oversight Committee urged the Justice Department to interview or reinterview key witnesses and pursue allegations against two prominent men who associated with the disgraced financier.
Former Miami Beach mayor Philip Levine and French celebrity hairstylist Frederic Fekkai both deny allegations of sexual assault – referred to federal prosecutors by the committee in June – from Epstein's longtime assistant Sarah Kellen.
The report also called for further questioning of another longtime Epstein assistant, Lesley Groff, over her possible knowledge of his crimes.
Groff maintained she had never suspected Epstein of sexually abusing women and girls – testimony the Republican investigators described as not credible.
The recommendations emerged from a 15-month congressional investigation involving testimony from prominent figures in Epstein's financial and social circle and an extensive examination of government and banking records.
"Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims," committee chairman James Comer said.
The report concluded that Epstein's crimes after 2005 could have been prevented had federal investigators and prosecutors pursued the original allegations against him more aggressively.
Instead, prosecutors in Florida reached a controversial agreement in 2007 allowing him to escape federal charges in exchange for pleading guilty to lesser state offences.
Epstein received an 18-month jail sentence but served only 13 months, enjoying extensive work-release privileges during which he continued abusing women, according to the report.
The investigation also accused financial institutions of overlooking suspicious transactions and warning signs of human trafficking, singling out American Express.
Lawmakers urged the Treasury Department to examine whether banks were properly reporting suspicious activity linked to trafficking and money laundering.
The report also criticised the Justice Department for exposing survivors' private information during releases of Epstein files.
The Republican investigators said they had uncovered no evidence implicating Trump in Epstein's crimes and accused Democrats of politicising the inquiry.
But the committee's top Democrat, Robert Garcia, dismissed the findings as the product of an incomplete investigation that included no public hearings, accusing the Justice Department of illegally withholding "over 2.5 million pages of documents."
Democrats, who seized control of Congress in last week's midterm elections, have vowed to continue investigating Epstein's network when they assume their new powers in January.
Epstein died in a New York jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges. His accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell is serving a 20-year prison sentence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Content Forum moots regional safeguards
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SOUTHEAST Asian countries should adopt common minimum safeguards to protect children from commercial risks in the digital economy.
Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia chief executive officer Mediha Mahmood said these should include having clearer advertising disclosures and preventing under-18 creators from being paid to promote age-restricted products.
Content Forum put forward the proposals at the Asean ICT Forum on Child Online Protection in Manila last week.
Mediha said children's growing involvement in the digital economy had exposed them to commercial risks that were often overlooked.
"Follow the money and you begin to see the risks differently. Money can be made from children, through children, and even used to gain access to them.
"When the commercial incentives are this powerful, protecting children cannot be left to parents and children alone."
Mediha spoke during a panel discussion titled "Behind the Feed", which examined child safety in digital advertising and the influencer ecosystem.
Content Forum identified three areas for regional cooperation: clearer advertising disclosures that children can understand; safeguards against commercial targeting involving age-restricted products; and, safer brand collaborations through official channels, supported by platform measures to prevent grooming and exploitation.
Mediha also highlighted Malaysia's efforts to address these risks through the recently registered fourth edition of the Content Code, as well as Content Forum's proposed Influencer and Brand Collaboration Guidelines and Gaming Sub-Code.
These initiatives cover children's privacy, advertising transparency, protection for young creators, age-appropriate gaming and safer online interactions.
Both proposed instruments have completed public consultations, which drew feedback from local and international industry players, creators, the public and child advocacy organisations, including the United Nations Children's Fund and Ecpat, a global network of civil society organisations.
Mediha said the Asean Regional Plan of Action and the Asean Industry Working Group could provide avenues to advance the proposals.
"The feed doesn't recognise national borders. The money certainly doesn't. A child should not have less protection simply because the brand, creator or platform they are dealing with is based in another country."

Title: Penang welcomes inaugural winter charter flight from Poland
Article:

PENANG has welcomed its first winter charter flight from Warsaw, marking a new addition to Malaysia's international air travel.
The flight, operated by Rainbow Tours using a 293-seat Boeing 787 Dreamliner, was part of the company's winter charter programme running from this month to March next year.
The seasonal direct service will operate once a week, providing greater accessibility for Polish holidaymakers visiting Malaysia during the European winter season.
The passengers were welcomed in a ceremony jointly organised by Penang Global Tourism (PGT) and Tourism Malaysia, together with tourism stakeholders and industry partners.
Among those present to welcome them were Polish embassy counsellor Mateusz Reszczyk, Honorary Consul of Poland in Penang Datuk Seri Suppiah Manikam and Tourism Malaysia deputy director-general (promotions II) Lee Thai Hung.
Tourism Malaysia said the service reflected growing interest among Polish travellers in Malaysia's cultural heritage, tropical islands, nature-based attractions and gastronomy.
"The direct connection is expected to boost Penang's tourism sector. Poland has emerged as a promising source market for Malaysia within central and eastern Europe," it said.
Malaysia recorded 40,526 tourist arrivals from Poland, or an 8.3 per cent year-on-year increase, between January and September.
Tourism Malaysia said strategic partnerships with international tour operators were essential to expanding market reach and sustaining tourist arrivals under the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai had said last month the Warsaw-Penang service would serve as a stepping stone to establishing a presence in the European tourism market.

Title: Trump ally elected US House Republican leader after election rout
Article:
WASHINGTON: Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday, defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat.
Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, US media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority.
The Ohio congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's elections.
Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.
Jordan, a founding member of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, had pitched himself as the fighter Republicans need to confront Democrats during the final two years of Trump's presidency.
His victory represented a rejection of the party's established leadership, with Scalise having served in senior Republican positions for more than a decade.
Both men are staunch Trump allies, but the president declined to endorse either candidate.
The contest was a rematch of their 2023 battle for the speakership following the ouster of Kevin McCarthy.
Scalise initially won the Republican nomination but withdrew after failing to secure sufficient support, while Jordan subsequently lost three votes on the House floor before Johnson emerged as a compromise candidate.
Jordan, a former champion wrestler who has represented Ohio in Congress since 2007, built his reputation as a political brawler and fierce critic of the Republican establishment.
Former speaker John Boehner once branded him a "legislative terrorist" for his uncompromising tactics.
He also emerged as a leading defender of Trump during congressional investigations into the president's attempts to overturn his 2020 election defeat.
Thune's reelection as Senate Republican leader came after conservative lawmakers temporarily stalled proceedings, demanding a clearer strategy for confronting the incoming Democratic majority.
"I appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today," he said in a statement, adding that he was honored to retain their support.
Thune, who will become Senate minority leader in January, pledged to work with Trump and oppose Democratic efforts to enact what he called their "far-left, liberal agenda."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boeing to cut 5pc of commercial jet workforce
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SEATTLE: Boeing Commercial Airplanes plans to cut five per cent of its workforce as it struggles to increase jetliner production,  division chief Stephanie Pope told employees recently in an internal memo.
"As shared in our third-quarter earnings, we need to reset the pace of our production rate ramps to provide our factories and supply chain partners additional time to achieve stability.
"Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position," Pope said in the memo reviewed by Reuters.
The reductions will happen through attrition and involuntary layoffs, with notices going out next month at the earliest, according to the memo.
Boeing is required in many states to give workers 60 days' notice.
Boeing chief executive officer  Kelly Ortberg told analysts last month the company would miss its 737 jetliner production and delivery targets this year.
It now expects to reach a 737 production rate of 47 jets per month early next year, after previously projecting it would hit that pace by summer this year.
He also said the company does not expect to reach US$10 billion in free cash flow until 2029, a year later than analysts had expected.
That target is seen by investors as a critical milestone in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies that left Boeing with a dented reputation, heavily in debt and under stricter regulatory scrutiny.
Boeing's popular 737 narrow-body jet is its single largest cash generator, making higher output essential for the company's recovery.
Boeing has also struggled to increase production of its popular 787 wide-body jet from eight jets a month to 10 a month.
The Seattle-based commercial airplane division had 50,494 employees up to last December, according to the company's website. — REUTERS
